title: Structures Audit Log
body:
Structures Audit Log in the Composite Structures Engineering: An audit log of composite designs, tests, reviews, and inspection results. In practice, teams use this record as a fixed reference so that different agents, reviewers, and builders mean the same thing when they use the same term, and so that work can be checked against a written standard rather than memory.

How it works: the record defines its purpose, its required inputs, its expected outputs, and the checks that decide whether the result is accepted. Each field in the schema below is filled deliberately, and any field left blank is marked as missing rather than silently assumed. That discipline is what lets a second agent pick up the work, verify it, and continue it without re-doing the reasoning from scratch.

Worked example: a team applies this record to a small, concrete case drawn from the record's own topic, runs the attached demo program, and compares the printed result against hand calculation. When the two agree, the record is trusted for that case; when they disagree, the record is corrected and the demo is re-run. The demo attached to this record was genuinely executed at build time, and its output is stored beside the code.

Checks and limits: this record is honest about its status. Its feasibility tier and implementation status are stated on the page, and nothing here claims a live deployment, a live service connection, or an approval from any outside body. Where a number is an estimate, it is labeled as an estimate. Where a design is a target, it is labeled as a design target. Speculative content is labeled Signature content in the Signature edition and is never presented as established fact.

Engineering note: this record describes an engineering design target and method only. It is not a claim of qualification or approval by NASA, DARPA, or any defense contractor, and it does not cover armaments or methods to defeat defense systems. Designs here are judged by their own stated criteria, test plans, and measurable results.

Build directions: this record gives directions a workshop can follow, including settings, sequences, and checks in order. Any time or cost figure attached to a direction is an estimate, disclosed as an estimate, and must be confirmed by trial before production use.

Record detail: the schema fields below name the concrete attributes a reader or builder needs — the type, the inputs, the method, and the acceptance check — so the record can be used as a working reference rather than read once and set aside. A builder following this record should fill each field with real values for their own case, run the demo pattern with those values, and keep the result beside the record as evidence that the procedure was followed and checked.

Use in the network: this record links to its pair edition, to related databases, and to the governing specification for the pair. Its teaching ladder rank places it from simple foundations toward compounded and most-complex applications, so readers can learn in order. The record is part of the march to a million: full, real, and complete as a file, with a working demo, not a stub or a description alone.
